alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of an old printed title page. In capitals it reads "OF THOMAS MORLEY THE FIRST BOOKE OF BALLETTS TO FIVE VOYCES." Below is a woodcut of a rake, a two-pronged fork and a scythe crossed and tied with a ribbon, standing in a tuft of grass, with a curling scroll lettered "SED ADHVC MEA MESSI" and "IN HERBA EST". At the foot: "IN LONDON BY THOMAS ESTE.", a rule, and the year in Roman numerals, "CIↃ. IↃ. XC. V."
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de una antigua portada impresa. En mayúsculas dice "OF THOMAS MORLEY THE FIRST BOOKE OF BALLETTS TO FIVE VOYCES." Debajo hay un grabado en madera de un rastrillo, una horca de dos puntas y una guadaña cruzados y atados con una cinta, sobre una mata de hierba, con una filacteria enroscada que dice "SED ADHVC MEA MESSI" e "IN HERBA EST". Al pie: "IN LONDON BY THOMAS ESTE.", una raya y el año en números romanos, "CIↃ. IↃ. XC. V."

caption.en: The title page of the Cantus part-book of Morley's First Booke of Balletts to Five Voyces, printed in London by Thomas Este in 1595, the earliest known printing of Now is the month of Maying.
caption.es: La portada del libro de voces del Cantus de The First Booke of Balletts to Five Voyces de Morley, impreso en Londres por Thomas Este en 1595, la primera impresión conocida de Now is the month of Maying.

source: Thomas Morley, The First Booke of Balletts to Five Voyces (London: Thomas Este, 1595; RISM M 3697), Cantus part-book, title page (image n0); cropped to the printed panel inside the ornamental border

alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of a page of early printed music headed "III." and "CANTVS.", with a later handwritten "63." in the top corner. Six staves of diamond-headed notes begin with a large plain capital N, and the words under them read "Ow is the month of Maying, When merry lads are playing. Fa la ...", "Each with his bonny lasse, vpon the greeny grasse" and many more "Fa la"s. Below the music, two stanzas are printed as verse: "The spring clad all in gladnesse, Doth laugh at winters sadnesse. Fa la la. And to the Bagpips sound, The Nimphs tread out their ground. Fa la la." and "Fye then why sit wee musing, Youths sweet delight refusing. Fa la la. Say daintie Nimphs and speake, Shall wee play barly breake. Fa la la la."
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de una página de música impresa antigua con el encabezado "III." y "CANTVS.", y un "63." escrito a mano más tarde en la esquina superior. Seis pentagramas de notas con cabeza de rombo empiezan con una gran N mayúscula sin adornos, y la letra debajo dice "Ow is the month of Maying, When merry lads are playing. Fa la ...", "Each with his bonny lasse, vpon the greeny grasse" y muchos más "Fa la". Debajo de la música van dos estrofas impresas como versos: "The spring clad all in gladnesse, Doth laugh at winters sadnesse. Fa la la. And to the Bagpips sound, The Nimphs tread out their ground. Fa la la." y "Fye then why sit wee musing, Youths sweet delight refusing. Fa la la. Say daintie Nimphs and speake, Shall wee play barly breake. Fa la la la."

caption.en: No. III in the Cantus book of 1595: the large N begins "Now is the month of Maying", the first stanza runs under the notes with each half written out twice, and the other two stanzas are printed below as verse.
caption.es: El n.º III en el libro del Cantus de 1595: la gran N inicia "Now is the month of Maying", la primera estrofa va bajo las notas con cada mitad escrita dos veces, y las otras dos estrofas van impresas debajo como versos.

source: Thomas Morley, The First Booke of Balletts to Five Voyces (London: Thomas Este, 1595; RISM M 3697), Cantus part-book, No. III, "Now is the month of Maying" (image n7); cropped to the page

alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of six staves of early printed music with diamond-headed notes, headed "III." and "QVINTO." and beginning with a large swash capital S. The Italian words under them read "O ben mi c'ha bon tempo. ij. Fa la la la la la la.", "So ben mi c'ha bon tempo. ij.", "Al so ma basta mo. ij." and many "Fa la"s, ending "Fa la la la." Faint mirror-image print from the other side of the leaf shows through.
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de seis pentagramas de música impresa antigua con notas con cabeza de rombo, con el encabezado "III." y "QVINTO." y una gran S mayúscula de rasgos curvos al principio. La letra italiana debajo dice "O ben mi c'ha bon tempo. ij. Fa la la la la la la.", "So ben mi c'ha bon tempo. ij.", "Al so ma basta mo. ij." y muchos "Fa la", y termina "Fa la la la." Se transparenta tenuemente, al revés, la impresión del otro lado de la hoja.

caption.en: No. III in the Quinto book of Morley's Italian edition, printed by Thomas Este the same year: the same music, sung to "So ben mi c'ha bon tempo", the opening of Orazio Vecchi's song printed in Venice in 1590.
caption.es: El n.º III en el libro del Quinto de la edición italiana de Morley, impresa por Thomas Este el mismo año: la misma música, cantada con "So ben mi c'ha bon tempo", el comienzo de la canción de Orazio Vecchi impresa en Venecia en 1590.

source: Thomas Morley, Di Tomaso Morlei il primo libro delle ballette a cinque voci (In Londra: appresso Tomaso Este, 1595; RISM M 3698), Quinto part-book, No. III, "So ben mi c'ha bon tempo" (image n39); cropped to the music, leaving out the blank staves and the second stanza below

alt.en: A black-and-white microfilm image of seven lines of old printed text, with "Ballette." in the margin. It reads, in part: "There is also another kind more light then this, which they tearme Ballete or daunces, and are songs, which being song to a dittie may likewise be daunced" and "There be also an other kind of Ballets, commonlie called fa las, the first set of that kind which I haue seene was made by Gastaldi, if others haue laboured in the same field, I know not but a slight kind of musick it is, & as I take it deuised to be daunced to voices."
alt.es: Una imagen en blanco y negro, de microfilm, de siete líneas de texto impreso antiguo, con "Ballette." en el margen. Dice, en parte: "There is also another kind more light then this, which they tearme Ballete or daunces, and are songs, which being song to a dittie may likewise be daunced" y "There be also an other kind of Ballets, commonlie called fa las, the first set of that kind which I haue seene was made by Gastaldi, if others haue laboured in the same field, I know not but a slight kind of musick it is, & as I take it deuised to be daunced to voices."

caption.en: Morley's own account of the ballett in his A Plaine and Easie Introduction to Practicall Musicke (London, 1597), p. 180: "an other kind of Ballets, commonlie called fa las", "deuised to be daunced to voices".
caption.es: La descripción del ballett por el propio Morley en su A Plaine and Easie Introduction to Practicall Musicke (Londres, 1597), p. 180: "an other kind of Ballets, commonlie called fa las" (otra clase de balletts, llamados comúnmente fa las), "deuised to be daunced to voices" (ideada para bailarse con voces).

source: Thomas Morley, A Plaine and Easie Introduction to Practicall Musicke (London: Peter Short, 1597), "The third part", p. 180 (image n187); cropped to the seven lines on villanelle and balletts
